messages:
maria: New signup flagged a weird perf difference between Go and JS quickstart sample apps. Both call the same /v1/embeds pagination flow but Go seems to backpress earlier and stalls at ~6 concurrent pages while JS goes up to 20. User hit a long-run and thought our service throttled them.

theo: do we have logs from their run? sounds like client-side cap in Go runtime.

maria: pasted trimmed logs from the sample harness: 
```
2026-03-22T11:18:02Z worker-12 pageFetch start cursor=abc
2026-03-22T11:18:02Z worker-12 acquireToken -> ok
2026-03-22T11:18:02Z worker-12 http 200 latency=120ms
2026-03-22T11:18:02Z worker-12 pageFetch start cursor=def
2026-03-22T11:18:03Z throttle.global cap hit (6) blocking
2026-03-22T11:18:04Z http 429 backoff
```

priya: tl;dr: Go SDK enforces a global concurrency token pool by default, whereas JS uses per-cursor concurrency + a higher global limit. That explains the different breakpoints.

maria: exact. the onboarding quickstart uses SDK defaults and our docs show the JS snippet. New users on Go hit the stricter default and think the backend is flaky.

theo: oh no. SDK parity issue. We should align defaults and call it out in quickstart. Proposal: make both SDKs default to per-cursor maxConcurrency=8 and globalBurst=32 for sample apps. Also add a note on auth retry: Go currently retries auth refresh inline and can cause small thundering herds; JS queues refresh results so replays get serialized.

priya: suggested change list: 1) change Go default to per-cursor-aware limiter, 2) implement refresh result multiplexing in Go, 3) add a short migration note in quickstart and a link to a config snippet.

maria: sample config suggestion we can show in docs: 
```
// recommended quickstart client config
ClientConfig{
  PerCursor: { MaxConcurrency: 8, EnqueueTimeoutMs: 3000 },
  GlobalThrottle: { TokensPerSec: 50, Burst: 32 },
  Auth: { RefreshReplayWindowMs: 200, MultiplexRefresh: true }
}
```

infra-bot: CI: found 2 failing e2e tests in go-sdk/paginator due to changed timing assumptions.

theo: i'll open a parity PR to align defaults and add an opt-in flag for older clients. priya can drive the multiplex refresh patch. also add a small e2e that runs both quickstarts and asserts they can hit 16 concurrent pages without causing 429s in our local harness.

priya: will do. also request docs to add a "FAQ: why am I seeing throttling in Go quickstart" with an example of how to raise limits for batch migrations. @docs ptal.

docs: noted. will add the FAQ and update the quickstart snippets within today. i'll also add a short paragraph about replay/refresh behavior differences and a link to the new API toggle.

maria: thanks all. filing issue: https://redwood.ai/issue/4621 — please drop PR links here when ready. keeping this thread as the coordination channel. :white_check_mark:
